narrative.overview:
HOMCOM is shown the way a maker introduces a product: the shop's H in polished chrome, lit in its own studio, with real stock, real prices and the shop's live status around it. There are two themes and they are one world. Night is deep space ink lit by an ion light running from violet to blue, with warm amber kept for offers. Day is pale lavender-white with the same light turned low and violet glass ribbons passing through. Both are made of the same few materials: chrome, glass with a bright top edge, hairlines, and one typeface.

The stage belongs to the first viewport. From the catalogue down the page is an instrument: dense, ruled, price-led, built for a phone on weak data. Display lines are big and light (300 weight) and everything that does work is set heavier (550 to 700). Products without a photo are never given an icon. They get a rendered glass plate with the maker's name laid on the slab's face. Glass is used as a material with a job: it holds a product name, lifts a floating stock tile, or frames the header. It is never there just to blur things. Wherever someone reads, the surface is opaque.

The system was built to be cheap: one self-hosted font file, rasters of 4 to 7 KB, a live map that loads only when asked for, and motion that runs on the compositor. Reduced motion, lite mode, high contrast and forced colours each strip back to a still, complete page.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes, one world: Night ink with ion light, Day lavender with the same light at low intensity.
One family, Hanken Grotesk, light for display and heavy for prices and controls.
Prices lead every product, in tabular lining figures.
Night surfaces are defined by their edge, Day surfaces by elevation.
Rendered glass plates stand in for missing photos, with the words set in the slab's plane.
Ruled rows, not boxes, for services, contact lines, specs and facts.
Pills for every control. Generous rounded rectangles for surfaces.

rules.name: The Amber Means Offer Rule
rules.body: Amber marks a price that has come down and nothing else. Low stock and refurbished use the warn yellow, and decoration never uses amber.

rules.name: The Measured Pair Rule
rules.body: No text colour ships until its ratio has been measured against the surface it sits on, in both themes. Write the ratio next to the token.

rules.name: The Ours, Not Theirs Rule
rules.body: A WhatsApp button is the page's own primary action, in the Launch gradient. The label and the logo say which app it is. No brand green.

rules.name: The Name, Then Price Rule
rules.body: On every product surface the name comes first and the price sits directly under it, the largest figure on the card. Under the price comes what the product was and what that saves, or "incl. VAT". Every figure that lines up (prices, totals, counts, hours, badges) uses `tabular-nums lining-nums`.

rules.name: The Light Voice, Heavy Hands Rule
rules.body: Big type is light (300–350). Anything you act on or compare is 550 or heavier. Never set a display line bold.

rules.name: The Light Runs On Rule
rules.body: The hero's light does not stop at the first screen. Every section below is lit from the top right, by a still drawing of the hero's streaks at Night and of its glass ribbons by Day. Words placed in that light keep their measured contrast. It is painted once with the section and never moves with the scroll.

rules.name: The Photo Earns Width Rule
rules.body: A product with a real photo takes two columns, photo beside a short fact list, only in the shop's own (featured) order. Sorted by price or name, every product takes one cell, so the order reads straight. On phones the wide card becomes a full row with the photo on top and no facts.

rules.name: The Edge or Lift Rule
rules.body: A surface is defined by an edge at Night and by elevation by Day, never both. A Night card has no drop shadow. A Day card has no hairline.

rules.name: The Opaque Reading Rule
rules.body: Any panel someone reads in is opaque: the modal, search, drawer, compare bar, phone nav and repair panel. Translucent, blurred glass is kept for small floating things (header, stock tiles, media tags). On touch screens and in lite mode it falls back to solid colour, because blur behind moving content is the most expensive thing a phone can scroll.

rules.name: The One-Thing Plate Rule
rules.body: A plate says the brand large with the model under it. With no brand, it says only the one spec that defines the product ("65W", "2m", "8-in-1", "Case + Glass"), never the title again and never an icon. Phone cards carry the lead alone.

rules.name: The Words on Glass Rule
rules.body: The plate's words are laid on the slab's front face in CSS 3D (`.plate-face`), using the renderer's own camera and each plate's turn (`--plate-ry`), so they recede with the glass. If a plate is re-rendered, its `--plate-ry` follows it. Without container-query units the words sit flat in the slab's lower left.

rules.name: The Map on Request Rule
rules.body: The live map loads only when someone taps for it. Until then an inline SVG sketch of Tom Mboya Street, in theme tokens, marks the shop and the building opposite.

dos: Do write every new colour as a token in both `:root`/`[data-theme="dark"]` and `[data-theme="light"]`, with its measured AA ratio in a comment.
Do lead every product surface with the price in 650 weight and tabular lining figures.
Do give a new surface a hairline and lit top at Night and a soft two-layer shadow by Day, never both.
Do make any panel someone reads in opaque (`--glass-solid` or `--card-solid`).
Do use rows divided by hairlines for lists of facts, services and contact lines.

Do animate only transform and opacity, with `--ease-out` (`cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)`) for arrivals and `--ease-sheet` for drawers and sheets. Start from a visible default, so nothing depends on a script to appear.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion` (everything simply there, the H still turns under a finger), `html.lite` (no canvas, no blur, no drift), `prefers-contrast` and forced colours.
Do keep every tap target at least 44px on touch and every field at 16px.
Do draw icons from the inline Phosphor sprite only.
donts: Don't put a category label, eyebrow or kicker above a title. The heading carries itself.
Don't number repair services or any other rows (01–04) when the order carries no information.
Don't put spec chips on product cards. Facts belong in the wide card's ruled list or in the pop-up.
Don't colour WhatsApp buttons in WhatsApp green.
Don't imitate the glass plates with CSS gradients or blur. Plates are rendered rasters with recorded provenance.
Don't edit the section light's SVGs by hand, or make it move with the scroll. Change tools/light/trails.js and run it.
Don't let black or navy into the Day chrome's reflection. Day darks are ribbon violet.
Don't use amber for anything but offers and savings.
Don't give a photo product a wide card outside the shop's own sort.
Don't add a second typeface, a monospace or a bold display line.
Don't load the live map, or any other heavy embed, before it is asked for.
